title: Pregnancy Recipes: Iron-and-Folate Bowls You Can Cook in 30 Minutes
excerpt: Three tasty recipes pairing heme/non-heme iron with vitamin C — Vietnamese-inspired bowls with clear amounts and food-safety notes.
content:
## Introduction
During pregnancy, it's essential to provide the body with sufficient iron and folate. Iron helps create red blood cells, while folate supports the development of the fetus. However, finding recipes rich in iron and folate can be a challenge. In this article, we'll introduce three simple and delicious recipes that combine iron with vitamin C, making it easy for expectant mothers to supplement the necessary nutrients.

## Nutrient Analysis
Iron and folate are two crucial nutrients during pregnancy. Iron helps prevent anemia, while folate supports the development of the fetus's brain and spine. Vitamin C also plays a vital role in enhancing iron absorption. Below are three recipes that combine iron with vitamin C:

* Recipe 1: Grilled Chicken and Vegetable Bowl
 + 100g grilled chicken (iron: 1.5mg)
 + 100g mixed vegetables (vitamin C: 50mg)
 + 1 cup cooked white rice
* Recipe 2: Beef and Water Spinach Stir-Fry Bowl
 + 100g beef stir-fry (iron: 2.5mg)
 + 100g water spinach (vitamin C: 30mg)
 + 1 cup cooked white rice
* Recipe 3: Grilled Fish and Salad Bowl
 + 100g grilled fish (iron: 1.2mg)
 + 100g mixed salad (vitamin C: 40mg)
 + 1 cup cooked white rice

## Food Safety Notes
During pregnancy, expectant mothers need to be mindful of food safety to avoid health risks. Below are some essential notes:
* Avoid eating raw or undercooked meat
* Avoid eating raw or undercooked fish
* Avoid eating raw or undercooked eggs
* Wash vegetables and fruits thoroughly before consumption
* Cook meat and fish thoroughly before consumption

## Practical Tips
Here are some practical tips to help expectant mothers easily supplement iron and folate:
* Eat a varied and balanced diet
* Take iron and folate supplements
* Drink vitamin C-rich fruit juice
* Eat fresh fruits and vegetables

## When to Seek Help
If expectant mothers experience any of the following symptoms, they should seek help from their doctor:
* Anemia
* Fatigue
* Headaches
* Nausea

## References
* [WHO: Nutrition counselling during pregnancy](https://www.who.int/tools/elena/interventions/nutrition-counselling-pregnancy)
* [CDC: People at Risk: Pregnant Women — Food Safety](https://www.cdc.gov/food-safety/people-at-risk/pregnant-women.html)
* [NHS: Foods to avoid in pregnancy](https://www.nhs.uk/pregnancy/keeping-well/foods-to-avoid/)
* [Pregnancy Meal Planner](/planner) provides recipes rich in iron and folate for expectant mothers.

## Conclusion
The three recipes above combine iron with vitamin C, making it easy for expectant mothers to supplement the necessary nutrients. However, it's essential to be mindful of food safety and seek help from a doctor if any symptoms of anemia or other health issues arise.
